source: Quiz 3 - Sessions 1-4: Model Size, Thinking, and Skills
question: Beyond memory and task tracking, what 'less obvious' capability did the lecture say a harness gives an agent?

options.text: Command-line tools such as bash, run across many files
options.feedback: The lecture singles this out: a harness lets an agent compose filtering and extraction steps across many files, and it argues models have become unusually good at writing those commands. A chat session has no files to point them at.

options.text: A much bigger context window that holds more of the conversation
options.feedback: That is a property of the model and its limits, not something the surrounding harness supplies. The capability highlighted was reaching outside the conversation, to files and tools.

options.text: Direct access to the model's training data for looking facts up
options.feedback: A model does not consult its training data as a searchable store, and a harness does not give it one. What the harness adds is access to files and tools outside the model.

options.text: Faster token generation, so that long tasks finish sooner
options.feedback: Speed is not what a harness changes. The point was that an agent can reach for command-line tools and a file system, which a chat session cannot use at all.
